evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Creating a new game is a foundational, self-contained action and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators by giving them a game URL inherently requires a game to exist first (game creation).

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round requires a game/session context to exist first (a game must be created).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing all items tried this session requires that items have been added or rounds started (items must exist).

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item to estimate inherently requires that items exist (must be able to add items first).

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item is self-contained and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item requires that an item already exists (depends on ability to add items).

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item inherently requires that items exist (depends on adding/importing items).

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates requires the estimation process and estimates to be present (rounds/estimators must exist).

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires that estimates have been collected in a round (depends on round/estimation functionality).

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling requires the mechanism to collect and detect estimator cards (depends on the estimation/display behavior).

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate assumes an estimation round has taken place and an item is being estimated.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a previously estimated story requires that story to have been estimated earlier in the session (depends on prior rounds).

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste import is self-contained and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games requires that games are created and stored first (depends on game creation/storage).

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript requires that a game and its transcript exist (depends on game creation/storage).

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript requires that the transcript exists (depends on the ability to view/store game transcripts).

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript depends on transcripts being available (depends on transcript/view functionality).

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game requires that games exist and are stored (depends on game creation/storage).

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is a self-contained feature and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in requires the existence of an account (depends on account creation).

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details requires that an account exists (depends on account creation).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account inherently requires an account to exist first (depends on account creation).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Displaying dates/times in local timezone is self-contained UI/formatting and does not inherently require another story.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder requires accounts and stored credentials (depends on account creation and storage).

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Selecting estimation card sets presumes an estimation feature/round exists (depends on round/estimation functionality).

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Limiting invites depends on the invitation mechanism (inviting via game URL) being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via a received URL presumes an invitation mechanism that provides a game URL (depends on invite feature).

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the current item requires an active estimation round and item presentation (depends on rounds/items).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: This requires that items for the session exist (depends on adding/importing items).

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Seeing individual estimator activity presumes estimators can join and the estimation mechanism exists.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Being shown all estimates relies on the estimation process and participants giving estimates (depends on rounds and estimators).

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate until completion presumes the estimation/draw completion mechanics exist (depends on round/estimation behavior).

evaluations.evidence: be able to see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Showing prior estimates requires storing historical estimates and navigation to prior rounds (depends on history/scrolling functionality).

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Displaying who gave which estimates requires the estimation display/identity features (depends on immediate-estimate visibility/joining).

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared countdown timer is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another specific backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Auto-resetting the timer on completion depends on detecting when all estimators have played (estimation completion logic).

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling back through prior rounds requires prior rounds and stored estimates to exist (depends on rounds/storage).

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Maintaining consistent card ordering is an internal UI requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Allowing changes until draw completion presumes the draw/completion semantics and estimation mechanism exist.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail is a UI feature and does not inherently require another specific backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a non-functional requirement and is self-contained relative to other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing a glossary is self-contained and does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Creating indexes is a technical task not inherently dependent on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Browser compatibility is a non-functional requirement and does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: have the site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a cross-cutting non-functional requirement and not inherently dependent on another story.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance responsiveness is a standalone non-functional requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a self-contained requirement and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is an independent usability requirement and does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error page design is self-contained and not inherently dependent on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Specifying anonymized storage is a data/privacy requirement and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Providing usage metrics depends on collecting and storing usage/game data (requires game creation/storage and data collection).
